Lab 1 · Exercise 3 · SC-5009

Configure AI Project
Access & Guardrails

Learn how to control who can work inside Foundry projects, create blocklists to stop confidential terms from leaking through AI, and configure content filters that protect both inputs and outputs.

Microsoft Foundry Blocklists Content Filters 3 Tasks · ~30 min
In this exercise
01Manage Access within Foundry Projects 02Create and Manage Blocklists 03Configure and Refine Content Filters
What is this exercise about? Your organisation needs to control who can work inside AI projects and enforce restrictions on what content your AI can process or generate. In this exercise you will assign project-level roles, create a blocklist to prevent confidential terms from appearing in AI interactions, and set up a content filter policy that catches harmful content before it reaches users.
👥
Task 1
Manage Access within Foundry Projects
Resource-level access controls who can reach the Foundry resource, but project-level access controls what they can do inside it. In this task you assign a role at the project level, giving a specific user access to work within your AI project.
💡 Resource access vs project access
Think of the Foundry resource as the building and the project as a specific office inside it. A user might have a key card to enter the building (resource access) but still need a separate badge to enter your team’s office (project access). Both layers matter.
1
Open Microsoft Edge and go to https://ai.azure.com. Sign in using the credentials from the Info tab (ⓘ) in your lab instructions.
2
Click Start building. When prompted, create a new project with a unique name. Expand Advanced options to confirm the Foundry resource, region, subscription, and resource group. Click Create and wait for the project to be ready.
💡Close any Welcome window that appears after the project is created.
3
Once your project loads, find the New Foundry toggle in the top bar and disable it. If prompted, select Continue without feedback.
📝You need the classic experience to access the Management Center where user management lives.
4
In the left sidebar, scroll to the bottom and click Management center. Under Resource in the sidebar, click Users to view resource-level users.
5
Now under Project in the left sidebar, click Users. On the Manage users in this project page, click + New user.
6
In the Add resource users dialog, type your username in the New user field. In the Role dropdown, select Azure AI User. Click Add.
💡Find your username on the Info tab (ⓘ) in your lab instructions.
✅Your username is now assigned the Azure AI User role at the project level. This gives them access to work within the project without needing resource-level admin rights.
🚫
Task 2
Create and Manage Blocklists
The compliance team has provided terms that should never appear in AI interactions — internal codenames and confidential product names. You will create a blocklist in Microsoft Foundry that prevents those terms from being processed or generated by AI. Blocklists handle specific known terms, while content filters (Task 3) handle categories of harmful content.
💡 What is a blocklist?
A blocklist is a list of specific words, phrases, or patterns that your AI should never say or respond to. If a user sends a message containing a blocked term, the request is rejected before it ever reaches the model. If the model’s response would contain a blocked term, it’s caught before it reaches the user. Two match types are available: Exact match (the exact string) and Regex (a pattern, like anything starting with "Contoso").
1
In the left sidebar, click Go to project to return to your project overview. Then under Protect and govern, click Guardrails + controls.
2
On the Guardrails + controls page, select the Blocklists tab and click + Create blocklist.
3
On the Create a blocklist page, enter:

• Name: ConfidentialProjectTerms
• Description: Blocks internal codenames and confidential product terms.

Click Create blocklist.
4
Click into your new blocklist to open it. Select + Add new term. Make sure Exact match is selected, enter ProjectNova, then click Add term. Repeat for Starlight and Orion-x.
5
Click + Add new term again, but this time select Regex. Enter Contoso\w+ and click Add term. Review the blocklist to confirm all four terms appear.
📝The pattern Contoso\w+ matches anything starting with "Contoso" followed by one or more characters — for example ContosoVault or ContosoApp. This is more flexible than listing every product name individually.
✅You’ve created a blocklist with 3 exact match terms and 1 regex pattern. Any AI interaction containing these terms will now be blocked at the guardrail layer.
🛡️
Task 3
Configure and Refine Content Filters
Blocklists handle specific terms. Content filters handle entire categories of harmful content — violence, hate, sexual content, self-harm — and apply to both what users send to the model and what the model sends back. You will create a content filter policy called ContosoAIContentPolicy that sets severity thresholds and attaches your blocklist to both input and output.
💡 Input filter vs output filter
Input filter — checks what the user sends to the model. If a message contains violent or hateful language above the threshold, it’s blocked before the model even sees it.

Output filter — checks what the model sends back. Even if a prompt slips through, the output filter catches harmful content in the response before it reaches the user. Both layers together create defence in depth.
1
From the blocklist view, click the back arrow next to ConfidentialProjectTerms to return to Guardrails + Controls. Select the Content filters tab, then click + Create content filter.
2
On the Add basic information page, enter ContosoAIContentPolicy as the name. Click Next.
3
On the Set input filter page, set all four categories to Medium severity:

• Violence: Medium
• Hate: Medium
• Sexual: Medium
• Self-harm: Medium

This blocks both moderate and highly severe content while allowing mild content through.
4
Scroll down on the same page to the Blocklist section. Toggle it on. Under Select built-in or customized blocklist, select both Profanity and ConfidentialProjectTerms. Click Next.
5
On the Set output filter page, set all four categories to Medium severity — same thresholds as the input filter. This ensures the model’s responses are held to the same standard as the user’s inputs.
6
Scroll down to the Blocklist section of the output filter. Toggle it on and select Profanity and ConfidentialProjectTerms again. Click Next, then skip the deployments page, review the configuration, and click Create filter.
✅You’ve successfully configured a content filter policy with severity thresholds for harmful content categories and blocklist enforcement on both inputs and outputs.
🎉

Exercise Complete!

You’ve set up all three layers of AI governance — project access control, custom blocklists for confidential terms, and a content filter policy covering both inputs and outputs. This is what responsible AI deployment looks like in practice.
